text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it actually does. Think of it like cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: the room still functions the same way, but it becomes much easier to find things and move around. The main goal is to boost readability, making the code clearer for yourself and for other developers who might work on it later. This often involves breaking long functions into smaller ones, renaming confusing variables, or removing duplicated logic. By tackling refactoring regularly, you pay off "technical debt"—the extra work created by quick, messy fixes. This proactive approach prevents small problems from growing into major maintenance headaches.
